## Description

A `Stack.Host` is integrated with a `Split.Column` only when it is the direct and only child of the column. In this scenario the primary column renders `Tabs`, and a tab renders the stack. The column does not set `disableStackIntegration`. The stack has to be an ordinary nested stack: it is shown inside the tab, with its own navigation bar, and it navigates there.

It guards against the stack asking the column to take it over. The column does not take over a stack that is not its direct child, so such a stack would not be shown at all.

## Note

- The scenario has to be rendered as the root of the app: import `TestSplitStackV5InTabs` as `Example` in `apps/App.tsx`. The Split is a top-level navigator, and the tests menu would push the scenario onto a stack.

## Steps

### Baseline

1. Start the app with **TestSplitStackV5InTabs** as its root.

   - [ ] The primary column shows a tab bar with the "Stack" and "Plain" tabs, and "Stack" is selected.
   - [ ] The "Stack" tab shows the "Nested root" screen with the navigation bar of the stack, titled "Nested root".
   - [ ] The secondary column shows "Plain column".
   - [ ] No error is logged.

2. Tap "Push Nested pushed".

   - [ ] "Nested pushed" is pushed inside the tab, with a back button in the navigation bar of the stack. The tab bar stays in place.

3. Tap "Pop".

   - [ ] The tab shows "Nested root" again.

---

### Switching tabs

1. Tap "Push Nested pushed", then select the "Plain" tab.

   - [ ] The "Plain" tab shows "Plain tab".

2. Select the "Stack" tab.

   - [ ] "Nested pushed" is still on top of the stack.
